Really, I cannot, because that's under the jurisdiction of the military justice system, the prosecutor's office in the military. So to this very day, I did not have the opportunity to find out who the perpetrators of the crime were, whether they were from the Drina Corps or from which formations. It's something that I cannot confirm. After the war, from the media, I found out that a crime took place. I don't know who the perpetrators were. I did not conduct any investigation about it. This is something that was published later, after the war, after the combat operations stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Superb-law-enforcement-professional, lets just look at that answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, speaking of "professional," that wasn't very professional and I think that Mr. Nicholls should refrain from making those kind of characterisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, it's the witness's but I'll move on. That's the way Mr. Karadzic and the witness have described this man in the statement, as a superb professional law enforcement officer, and that is why I referred to him that way, and it is perhaps a bit sarcastic the way I used it, but I'll move on, but I don't think it's a fair objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you found out about the crime after the war from the media; that's your truthful testimony here today? That's when you first found out about the crime, talking about, again, the execution of Muslim prisoners after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I said that after the war ended I found out from the media that in the sector of Srebrenica a crime had occurred. To this very day I don't know the reasons the perpetrators, the extent. There are a lot of manipulations, and I stand by what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. So during the war you did not know that this crime had occurred?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No. I was not informed along the line of reporting from any of my subordinates in my hierarchy that any crime had occurred during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, but regardless of who did or did not inform you, your answer is: No, you were not aware that this crime occurred during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Then at paragraph 36 of your statement you talk about being on the MUP staff in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P02981, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, before we get to that, your code in July 1995, your call-sign, was Tango 3; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I didn't understand the call-sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you referred to on radio communications as Tango 3? Tomo Kovac was Tango 2; the minister was Tango 1.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I cannot remember the code-name, my true call-sign during the war is Karlo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we have P06188, please, e-court page 2. We need to -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. In English we have head of RJB/public security department is Tango 3. Does that help refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: A little bit, but I don't recall anybody ever referring to me as "Tango 3" during any kind of communication. It's possible that this is some kind of call-sign directory of the ministry, but there is no introduction or a conclusion so that you could tell what this is, what kind of a paper this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- because here I can see --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's go to page 1 just so you can see what the document is. This is the Zvornik one, and just so you know Mane Djuric testified here that it was accurate as to his call-sign and to Danilo Zoljic's and to the Zvornik communication centre. So I'm just trying to see if you remember. You said it helps you remember a little bit or something that you were Tango 3.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I really cannot remember my call-sign. This is the first time that I'm looking at the UKT, ultra-short wave, directory of the Zvornik CJB. I was never in any kind of action where somebody - how can I put it? - would refer to me in communications as - how did you say it? - Tango 3. It's possible that I as a MUP civil servant was included in it and that the signals administration did assign code-names, but I wasn't aware of that. I'm surprised to see that I was Tango 3 because throughout for all the functions I was referred to as Karlo. I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- saying that this document is not valid. But I'm just saying, I mean, I don't really have any particular comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I won't tender this document now, Your Honour, because Tango 2 is coming --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not already admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll add this page to the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 36 you talk about how you spent most of the time in July 1995 at the RJB headquarters in Bijeljina, and you remember the MUP staff in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P02981, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This document is dated -- it's unclear but June 1995 and it's type-signed by Deputy Minister Tomo Kovac. You see your name there as number 2 on the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So this is the staff you're talking about, right, in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the staff, I'm here under number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to move on now, thank you, and talk about some of what the MUP knew at the beginning of the Srebrenica operation --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could have P04927, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, your copy's not to clear, unfortunately, but this is dated 6th July 1995, it's the RDB, so not your section, it's state security. And it's written in handwriting on the top right that it's for the VRS Army of Republika Srpska security department as well as going up to Bijeljina. And we see here in the top paragraph that there is a discussion of information learned on 6th July that Srebrenica representatives asked for a way to send Naser Oric in Tuzla back to Srebrenica. And at the bottom paragraph is what I'd like you to look at: "We will continue to monitor further developments of situation in Srebrenica battle-field through our sources and inform you about further developments in due time. We verbally informed the representatives of the VRS OB about the said information." Then it gives the source, Merkur, and personal observations of the operative. Information is classified as reliable, and this is from Goran Radovic. So again, not your subordinates, but you agree with me the RDB was monitoring the situation in Srebrenica on July 6th, 1995, the day of the attack?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I can say that this is a dispatch from the RDB. It's of a report nature and it's sent -- I cannot see all the places it is addressed to. I'm not sure, I couldn't see that. I don't see it --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- on my copy, it's difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I understand completely. I'll try to get a better version in the original. It says in the English that it goes to RDB centre Bijeljina. So you agree with me RDB is monitoring events in Srebrenica on 6 July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I can agree that they had information through this insider in terms of what was going on, but I cannot comment upon their dispatch in terms of what they were following and to what extent because this is the head of the RDB. I see that he has this information that things are happening there, but I'm not sure that he knows what will happen in the end. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- one of those pieces of information whereby they provide information to the RDB centre in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, just a second. It was sent by RDB Bijeljina, and according to the English version it was addressed to RS MUP, RDB Pale, 2nd and 3rd Administration. Can you tell us what it is about, 2nd and 3rd Administration of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is their organisation, which I wouldn't want to comment upon. It doesn't have to do with the public security section and I don't want to allow myself to comment upon things that I'm not familiar with and don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And I apologise for reading it out wrong. Could I have P04928.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. This is a much better copy. It states 6th of June on the top, but that's a typo because we can see right on the first sentence of the first paragraph that it's talking about early morning of the 6th July 1995. And this is sent from state security to Republika Srpska deputy minister of the interior personally and RS MUP RJB public security department personally. And the first couple lines state: "Early in the morning of 6 July 1995 representatives of the political and military leadership of Srebrenica established radio-contact with the leadership in Sarajevo. The Srebrenica representatives wanted some way to be found for Naser Oric to return to their area urgently (he is in Tuzla) ..." So the information we saw in the RDB document from 6 July that we just looked at from Goran Radovic up to Bijeljina --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And let's go to the next page, sorry -- or we can -- sorry, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- is now being sent on to you personally; correct? RS MUP RJB public security department personally, that's you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, that is I.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the information -- okay. Let's go to one more document P02985. Here we have 9 July a report from Vasic at the Zvornik CJB to the MUP in Bijeljina, talking about the situation on 9 July and saying where the units are advancing from towards Srebrenica, from Jadar towards Crni Guber, the villages of Salapovici and Ljubisavci have been occupied. And before I ask you the question I would like to now go to P05230. That's also a document. This one is from 10 July, the next day. This one is from deputy minister Tomo Kovac who's listed here as commander of the staff. And if you look at the third paragraph it also talks about capturing the villages of Salapovici and Ljubisavci and this document is at the Pale forces command staff. So again, just an example of how information in the field is conveyed to the Pale staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: According to dispatches -- actually, I'd like to read the previous one. It was a very poor copy, what I saw, so could it please be enlarged. Could I read one by one. You have shown me three dispatches, so let me read them at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: These two are separate. If you want to look at them again we can look at P02985, the one from Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Maybe we can put both B/C/S versions on the screen for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Take your time and read them, but my point very simply is this --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I cannot read Vasic's. Could Vasic's be enlarged. I've read Vasic's. Let me see the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I've read it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Very simply: Some of the information from Vasic's report, his dispatch, is being conveyed up to the Pale command staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. One more document, 65 ter 24707. This is dated 6th July, headed RS Ministry of the Interior police headquarters Pale, type-signed Tomo Kovac. And in the first paragraph not -- talking about the Herzegovina Corps it says between 50 and 100 enemy soldiers were killed and 23 captured on 5 July. And on page 2 of the English, please, if we could look at the bottom part: "In the early morning hours of 6 July 1995, the offensive against Srebrenica began, and we shall provide you with timely information on all interesting developments in that theatre of operations. "Staff commander. "Tomo Kovac." Okay. Are you ready for a question?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I can provide a comment now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you the question first. Now, this document talks about 50 to 100 enemy soldiers killed and 23 captured in a different location and says that all interesting developments in the theatre of the Srebrenica offensive will also be reported. Now, following the interesting developments in the theatre of operations of the Srebrenica operation, would the Pale forces command staff have found the execution of prisoners, even the taking of a large number of prisoners, an interesting development to follow?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I think, if I understood these dispatches correctly, police forces of Pale, the headquarters of the police forces in Pale, is the headquarters of the forces for the declared state of war in the zone of Sarajevo, not Srebrenica. That can be seen in the first dispatch that was established in June, I don't know the exact date, 1995. The headquarters were established because a strong Muslim offensive was launched against Serb positions around Sarajevo. A particularly key point is here between the Herzegovina Corps, let's say Trnovo and Treskavica, and in that area, in Trnovo, there were some units of police units that were resubordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska. And there was even a headquarters of the police forces in Trnovo there. This is reporting on losses, enemy losses, and an inaccurate figure is referred to or estimate, between 50 and 100, and that shows us that this has nothing to do with Srebrenica. And somewhere towards the bottom, Vasic -- I mean, it says that Vasic is reporting that some military operation is underway there and that certain positions had been reached. There is no reference to any kind of prisoner taking and other things that you're asking me about. My role at the headquarters in Pale, I can explain that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there. I'm not saying that that first page had anything to do with Srebrenica prisoners. Okay. The question is: Staff commander Tomo Kovac says at the end: "In the early morning hours of 6 July ... the offensive against Srebrenica began, and we shall provide you with timely information on all interesting developments in that theatre of operations." And the question was, I'll make it simpler: Would be the taking of a large number of Muslim prisoners an interesting development?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: We do not know here at all, on the basis of these dispatches, that there would be any prisoner taking in that military operation --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- that is conducted by General Mladic --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: From the dispatches --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not the question. Okay, I'll try to make it very simple. This is 6 July, all right, so there are no prisoners taken yet. We saw on the first page in a different area a report of enemy soldiers being captured. The question is, it's very simple: Since Tomo Kovac is saying he will provide information on all interesting developments in the Srebrenica theatre, would the taking in the future of large numbers of prisoners be an interesting development to report?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, but we did not receive that report as far as I can remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- that is why -- I mean, these are questions for Mr. Kovac as head of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, and if a report was made of large numbers of prisoners being taken was reported, would it also be an interesting development that large numbers of prisoners were executed by the VRS or the MUP in the Srebrenica theatre of operations?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: You're putting a hypothetical question to me which was not in the report. I as head of the department and a member of the staff in Pale, I did not receive any information about prisoner taking in Srebrenica, about the numbers, and I was not aware of any plan, believe me --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- so I cannot give any comments of prisoner taking in an operation that is conducted by the Army of Republika Srpska. The MUP of Republika Srpska is there with a minimal number of participants and has no powers over that act.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you testifying that you never received information that prisoner had been taken in the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I'm not sure now whether there is some dispatch. It really has been a long time that says that prisoners had been taken. In particular, I do not have a report and no one ever reported to me about any executions in certain locations. I do not have a single report like that as head of the RJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, again, that wasn't the question. The question was: You say you don't remember. Are you telling us that you don't remember whether you knew in July 1995, as head of the RJB, that the Serb forces had taken -- VRS and MUP had taken -- and/or MUP had taken large numbers of prisoners? Any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Don't [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Categorically, I had never been reported to about that. I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D6421, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, could I have P02992?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I take it you've seen this document before, you know about this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, but not a lot earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That means that I do not remember this document, although I was at headquarters. And as I gave a statement to the investigators of the MUP of Serbia when they first showed me this dispatch, my comment was that I cannot recall this order because I worked at Pale in relation to affairs that have to do with Sarajevo, not Srebrenica, because it was a staff that was dealing with Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. When was the first time you saw this document? Are you saying the first time you saw it, if I understand you, maybe I don't, is when the -- it was shown to you by the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Well, this is a document to the commander of the special police, you used to be a commander of, you weren't at the time, showing the supreme commander, Mr. Karadzic, has ordered -- issued an order for the engagement of the MUP. And I don't want to go through it all. At paragraph 2 it talks about the 1st Company of the PJP of Zvornik being engaged. In paragraph 3 it talks about Ljubisa Borovcanin being engaged to take part in combat in Srebrenica. So you never discussed or knew about this order on 10 July 1995; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you about this: It's type-signed by Tomo Kovac, and in an interview with -- in an interview in 2010 he confirmed that he neither signed nor approved this order, that's 65 ter 25299, e-court page 2 for my friends. And in his testimony in Serbia in the Medic case, Tomo Kovac testified at page 52 about this order: "I left this area, but the president of the republic directly called Karisik, my deputy, and Borovcanin and dictated to them this order." Now, does that help refresh your recollection? Tomo Kovac - and he's coming - basically says it was you who worked on this order with the president.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No, no. I refute Tomo Kovac's statement. I think he got things confused there. It's possible that the president orders someone on the staff because actually my signature is not there either, I did not sign this dispatch. There were many dispatches, you know, that's why I do not remember them, because this is one of the routine things as these things are written in the staff. A duty officer must have drafted a statement, or it's not a statement, but unskillfully. I was dealing with Sarajevo. I was not there. I was dealing with Sarajevo. As for the problems concerning Srebrenica, it's only Mr. Kovac who can speak about that so you can ask him when he comes. I deny this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Engaging the special police, not even now talking about anybody from Serbia, but engaging the special police to combat in Srebrenica theatre of operations, that's a routine matter?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I'm sure that I can tell you the following. The staff in Pale did its work and it was established for Sarajevo. I don't know how come now there is this story about this staff that is 200 kilometres away, that now it is also doing work in relation to Srebrenica --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, but --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- but Mr. Kovac headed the staff and I can give comments with regard to my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. You said this is a routine thing. Is engaging the special police on order of the supreme commander to take part in combat in Srebrenica combat a routine, just kind of nothing development?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Mr. Nicholls tell us what did the General say was a routine thing? He said that something else was routine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 66, line 1 -- lines 1 and 2. Can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand, which question? Could it kindly be repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm just going to move on. You say in your statement that on 10 July 1995 you met with President Karadzic, it's in his diary, I won't bring it up, for 20 minutes with Dragan Kijac, head of the DB. And you didn't discuss anything to do about Srebrenica when you met with the supreme commander on the day that the Supreme Command engaged the MUP in the Srebrenica operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Probably the protocol of the president is correct and I don't want to challenge that, but I cannot remember exactly - it's been a long time - what we talked about. But I assume that it only could have been my story about the Sarajevo theatre of operations and my duties to prevent a deblockade of our forces in that area and the fall of our positions. Because 150.000 civilians of Serb ethnicity --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- would be in peril.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So if I understand what you just answered now, you don't remember what you discussed, you can't say you didn't discuss Srebrenica, but you're assuming you talked about Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, because there's nothing else. I know what my task was on the staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- and that is Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, you answered --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: The problem --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, just before the break, three days after this order engaging Borovcanin as commander of these forces in Srebrenica, they murdered over a thousand Muslim prisoners in Kravica. You're aware of that, aren't you, that that attack happened three days after this order was issued?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Because I dealt with the question of Sarajevo on the staff in Pale that's what it was formed for. No one informed me about that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Last question. Until now, you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, we'll take a break, but before we take a break let me ask the witness this one. Since you were dealing with Sarajevo front, taking a high-profile policeman like Borovcanin and sending him to the -- another front, is something important to you such that you should have been informed of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot -- I mean, that is the remit of Mr. Kovac. He decides on who this commander is going to be. For us he was deputy commander of the special brigade and that is the only comment I can make. We were not planning anything important as far as Srebrenica is concerned, particularly not I who was dealing with the problem of Sarajevo and preventing a civilian exodus and planning evacuation -- a plan of evacuation and everything else that we were preparing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- so I really cannot comment on why Borovcanin -- I mean, Borovcanin did not have any kind of special task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you know at the time that Mr. Borovcanin was sent to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at the time. I learned of it only later, that he was at the head of a small unit which was under the command of the Drina Corps and it was dispatched there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is convenient, shall we take a break for 45 minutes, and resume at quarter past 1.00. One further thing. I asked around with the interpreters and the reporters, but given the timing we are minded -- the Chamber is minded to go till 3.30 today, if it is convenient with the parties as well, in order to conclude this witness's evidence today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We appreciate that very much, Mr. President. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.31 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we continue, shall we move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We are now in open session. In light of the discussion we had, we'll have -- we'll continue to hear the examination till 2.20 and we'll adjourn for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We were just talking about the 10 July order which, amongst other things, pulled Mr. Borovcanin and his units off the Trnovo front and it also engaged, according to the order, the 1st Company the PJP, special police unit, from Zvornik centre. And you said you didn't know anything about that at the time at all. Did you go to Zvornik the following day, 11 July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I think not. I cannot remember where I was on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, do you remember going down to Zvornik during the Srebrenica operation at all other than your trip on 16 July which we'll talk about later?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So when did you go besides the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I cannot remember going any other day, but as for the 16th, with the help of others I remember, because that was also a long time ago, that I went to the IKM, the forward command post, for the Zvornik Brigade for negotiations --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P06190, please, e-court page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: While this is coming up, I'll tell you what this is, sir. This is the diary of Mane Djuric who testified here and confirmed that it was his diary or notebook from the MUP. This is an entry that he confirmed was for 11 July 1995. We see at the top Goran S., then PJP special unit and then an arrow that says "can't." Predrag Blagojevic, Presidency, et cetera. Fuelling up. And then if you look towards the bottom: "Map for MUP. "MUP dispatch ...," some other things. And then it says: "Karisik - came by and expressed an interest." Again, this is a day after the 10 July order, putting the Zvornik PJP into the Srebrenica operation. Mane Djuric testified in this case, this is at T35037, line 19, about this entry: "All right. And below that we can see Karisik came by and expressed an interest. And just quickly in our interview you told us that must have been Milenko Karisik; correct?" And his answer was: "Most likely, yes." Does that help you refresh your memory that you went down to Zvornik the day the PJP from Zvornik were engaged?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I really cannot remember. It was a long time ago. I cannot. I mean, you know, it's been 20 years since then. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you have any special memory problems other than -- I don't want to get too personal, but you don't remember whether you went down to Zvornik on the day Srebrenica fell. I'm just asking if you have any particular memory problems for any other reason?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I don't know how much -- well, I don't have any proof from the doctors, if I may put it that way. But really, it was a long time ago and you're asking me about one day where I was 20 years ago. I'm not able to say because so much time has passed since then. I cannot do it. I'm sure this would be the case with many other people if you asked them to the day exactly on a particular day where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just for your reference, this is the day Srebrenica fell or was liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P4581, please. And I don't know if it will come up properly that way. It's also 65 ter 35025, tactical intercepts. Page 1 of the English, page 9, I believe, of the Serbian version. And I'll just say before this document wasn't on my list. I told Mr. Robinson that I planned to use it based on some earlier testimony and he agreed, so I thank him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right, sir, these are tactical intercepts, some of which have been authenticated by Mr. Mane Djuric. We can see that this is the 11th of July. The part I'm interested in is at the top, where it says: "They were collecting people who were left behind and it is possible have them -- and if it is possible have them wear green uniforms. Bor asked Omega 21 to check how many men he can collect. Karlo will take them." So again, just to help you remember, we've established that Omega 21 is Danilo Zoljic, who is the Zvornik centre commander of the PJP units. This is a day after Mr. Karadzic has ordered that the PJP units be engaged in Srebrenica. It's the same day that Mane Djuric wrote in his diary "Karisik came down and expressed an interest in it." And Bor is one of the code-names for commander Ljubisa Borovcanin. So the question is: Seeing that, does that help you remember whether you in fact went to Zvornik on the 11th of July and took an interest of the preparation of the PJP getting ready for the Srebrenica campaign?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No. I must give a comment. May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I am the head of a department. I do not get involved in the work of the centre chief. In his duties in terms of his jurisdiction, his duties to assemble forces pursuant to a dispatch, how he would organise that, and so on and so forth. Only if there are any problems in relation to the HQ, specific ones, then I could get involved and make suggestions. But in principle this was never requested nor ever needed. That's why I cannot give you any comments on these internal communications of theirs, nor do I remember them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, again the reason I brought this up now is we learned this morning from you that your code-name or nickname on the call-signs was Karlo. This is an intercept, including Karlo coming down. And Mane Djuric at the time wrote "Karisik came by."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I really cannot remember that. I am Karlo. I don't know if I stopped by or not. It's possible. But why would the commander of the PJP in the Zvornik headquarters be preparing any unit? This is something that I never did. It's not my practice. I'm the head of a department. This is not the sort of job that I'm doing. What it means was interested, I really do not know what does that mean. It is not my duty to prepare the Zvornik PJP units to act pursuant to a dispatch. No, I cannot confirm this. I simply cannot remember this. I never prepared this in any centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. But again, you're not just a civil servant like you keep saying, are you? You're head of public security; right? And this is a public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I agree. This is the centre activity in which I would never get involved. As to how they would activate a unit, whom they would assemble --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- this is something that I never did. This is something that belongs to the lower command ranks. It's part of the department, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now it's in your statement and I don't think there's any dispute, the night of the 11th you met with Mr. Karadzic again late at night, correct, 10.30 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Probably if it is written down, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So it's -- in the diary that day, the day after the MUP are engaged in the Srebrenica operation, the day Srebrenica falls, this is around the time of the end of the second Hotel Fontana meeting, you may or may not have been at Zvornik, you don't remember. But your testimony is you didn't discuss Srebrenica whatsoever with Mr. Karadzic that night? That's what it says in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes. I did not speak with the president about Srebrenica for sure because I had no information. I said that I was at the staff in Pale on the 11th, and I was conducting completely different activities related to the Sarajevo front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now let's look at a little bit of your testimony that you had no information about Srebrenica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Nicholls. The e-court says this intercept was not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour. I would tender it, although he has not said it's him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can mark it for identification, following our practice. But could the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark this entry for identification, following our practice. Shall we assign the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI P4581, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have P02996, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is a document dated 12 July, 1995. It's from Dragomir Vasic. It's to the MUP of RS, to the police force staff Bijeljina, office of the Minister Pale and the public security department, which is your department. Now, I don't want to spend a lot of time on this document, but it says that Mr. Vasic was at a meeting that morning with General Mladic and General Krstic -- well, it doesn't say that. It says a meeting with General Mladic and Krstic was held at the Bratunac Brigade. Paragraph 2 says the -- paragraph 3 says the military operation is continuing according to plan. Paragraph 5 talks about a meeting will begin soon, at 10.00 at which an agreement will be reached on the evacuation of the civilian population from Potocari. Paragraph 6 says the joint police forces are advancing on Potocari with the aim of taking UNPROFOR personnel prisoner, surrounding the entire civilian population, and clearing the terrain of enemy groups. Paragraph 8 says you will be promptly informed of all further facts and developments, and you head of the public security department are listed on this document. So do you stand by now your assertion that you didn't receive any information about Srebrenica so you couldn't discuss it with Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by my previous statement. This is reporting to the public security sector, informing Mr. Vasic who is the head of the public security centre. But you can see that the -- the minister of the interior would be the one authorised to take measures regarding the combat. As the head of the department, I was more turned towards civilian affairs and the regular tasks of the MUP and other activities that fall under the remit of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were engaged there as police, small number of us --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- we were resubordinated to the army and this is where our jurisdiction ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you to keep your -- try to focus a little bit more on my questions. First of all, this is not information to informing Mr. Vasic, as you said; this is information from Vasic, it's going to the public security department. You are head of the public security department; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, but not only to me. This is a regular report to Vasic and the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: He is the head of the sector and he needs to report to the department and the minister. I don't see anything of dispute there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P02986, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is a document dated 12 July 1995, it's from head of RDB, Dragan Kijac. It's to the deputy minister of the interior of the RS, that's Tomo Kovac, personally. And it's to head of the RJB/RS MUP Bijeljina personally, which is you. And it states in paragraph 1 referring to a report from UN military observers, that by 1700 hours about 60.000 refugees left Srebrenica for the north and their overall position will be hopeless in 48 hours. All right. This is going to you personally; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: According to the dispatch, yes. This is regular report. The department to the minister and to the department as the head of -- and myself as the head of the department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. And contrary to what you said earlier, this is reporting on Srebrenica; correct? It's telling you that the situation for the refugees is hopeless?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I'm saying again my jurisdiction was not to take over military operation conducted --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop, stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- by the VRS --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There was no part of my question that said whether you were or not meant to take over an operation from the VRS. My question was: You received this information and you did receive this information and you knew this information; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Probably, since there is this dispatch then it probably means that it did reach the department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, again - and I don't say this sarcastically - you're a highly ranked, highly decorated, highly promoted, in your own words, superb professional. So presumably you read dispatches about a significant military operation that are directed to you personally; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: As a professional, I'm saying that my public security department in all procedures receives dispatches from those sent in the form of regular reports which appear and infrequently from the state security sector about things that they are reporting about. So my comment is nothing else other than that that dispatch was sent. Probably it reached the public security department, but my own personal jurisdiction was not to act --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, stop --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- and for me to make decisions --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. I'm only asking if you got it and read it, not what you did afterwards or what your duty was.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I'm sure that the dispatch arrived, but I'm not sure if I read it or not since I had many other duties at that time as the head of the department, not just to read that dispatch which, to be honest, I am now here for the first time, and when you present it perhaps I can recollect it a little bit because situations were infrequent, excuse me, when information and reports were received from the RDB, intelligence reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately I have very little time, or I could go through very many documents from the RDB to you which are in evidence in this case. I'll go through a couple more, P04936. This is the same day, 12 July. So if they're infrequent, it's interesting that you are getting lots of them during the Srebrenica operation. And you can think about that and I'll ask you about it. Now, this document which again is to you personally as head of RJB from the head of the RDB, Dragan Kijac, states that the humanitarian situation according to reports they know about are worse than ever in Srebrenica. There are 30.000 people in and around the DutchBat base. There are about 8.000 people trying to reach UNPROFOR base and there is not a single military -- a single armed soldier of the so-called BH army among these people. Now, I'm not asking about your duty, your jurisdiction, or anything other than than, again, you are receiving information about events in Srebrenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: This information obviously, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So it was not correct when you stated a little while ago that it would have been impossible for you to discuss Srebrenica events with Radovan Karadzic when you met with him because you were receiving information about Srebrenica and you were the head of the RJB; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I did not speak about Srebrenica with President Karadzic, I'm sure about that. The only thing that we could have talked about was the Sarajevo, since I was at the staff in Pale, it was the Sarajevo front because I was personally entrusted with that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, okay, okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: This is something that arrived at the department in Bijeljina and at the time I was in Pale.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat what he said. He overlapped with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if you permit me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, you totally overlapped with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said the witness is trying to say where he was and where the telegrams were arriving, and Mr. Nicholls keeps interrupting him. He should be allowed to say what he's saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- manage to do all of that in the re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's your problem, Mr. Karadzic. The witness was not answering the question posed -- put by the counsel of the Prosecution. I don't think -- I don't find any problematic conduct in Mr. Nicholls' cross-examination. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, P04389, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, earlier today at page 64 I asked you: "Are you telling us that you don't remember whether you knew in July of 1995 as head of the RJB that the Serb forces had taken, VRS and MUP had taken -- and/or VRS or MUP had taken large numbers of prisoners, any prisoners?" "A. No." Take a look at this document, please, this is the next day, 13 July. You said these are very rare, I want to know what you mean by "rare" that you got these types of informations from the DB. 13 July 1995 to RS deputy minister of the interior personally, that's Tomo Kovac; and to you, head RS MUP Bijeljina, public security department, personally: "During the night of 12-13 July 1995, members of the VRS, Army of Republika Srpska, and MUP managed to capture a large number of Muslim soldiers (over 300) in ambushes set up in the general Konjevic Polje area." Below that in the same paragraph, sir: "The operation to detect and neutralise Muslim groups is continuing. Earlier information regarding their intentions on the access of movement towards Kladanj ..." I'll skip the locations "has been confirmed many times in interviews with prisoners." And then it talks about taking custody of one of the prisoners. So you were incorrect when you said earlier this morning that you didn't receive any information about the army and/or MUP taking prisoners during the Srebrenica campaign; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to say that at that time I was in Pale at the staff and turned to the Sarajevo problems. These dispatches were arriving at the head of the -- at the seat of the department in Bijeljina, which is some 250 to 300 kilometres away. And at that moment I could not read these dispatches because I was dealing with specific problems in the Sarajevo area as a member of the staff in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So your testimony is that the - I have to say it - superb professionals of the RS MUP in July 1995, this is not the beginning of the war, when the head of state security sends you personally a series of documents about events in Srebrenica, you don't read them? And the reason you don't read them is because you're 200 kilometres away from where they are sent to, that's your story? These are sent by Telex. These are sent through the air. They can't be forwarded to you? They can't be couriered to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, how many questions is there that the witness can answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's basically one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Put it simply then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is is pretty simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There is no way these could have reached you, is that your testimony? That's why you didn't read them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: One of the reasons why I didn't read them on time was the fact that I was far away and technical possibilities -- I mean territorially I was very far away at a different destination, Sarajevo, as I've already mentioned, resolving the problems of the staff that was working on Sarajevo, as I've already explained. And these reports, as far as I'm concerned, are of the nature of the documents that they sent to the minister and to me personally. I'm not denying that these dispatches exist, but as you can see I cannot see in this dispatch anything about any kind of execution or a plan for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, now I'm going to stop you --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- then or later I did not --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now I'm going to stop you. The question was about taking prisoners. You keep saying you didn't know about executions, when I'm not asking you if you knew about executions. So let me just go here now. In the professional MUP chain, we can see this reporting, I've shown Dragomir Vasic reporting on the same day it getting up the chain. We see state security carrying out interviews with prisoners, getting information, and forwarding it to you. Is -- was President Karadzic a professional? Was he conscientious? Or was he just sort of somebody who would say, "I'm in Pale, I don't know what the hell is going on, I don't care"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: As head of the department, I was not supposed to report to the president about this. This is the top of the ministry, I'm referring to the then-minister. If anybody was supposed to report to him about this kind of knowledge, then it should have been that gentleman within his own duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Tomo Kovac should have reported all this to the president when he met with him on 13, 14, and 15 July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I don't know when he met with him and I cannot comment upon what the minister did, but you are asking me whether I had to report to President Karadzic. No, it's the top of the MUP, the minister himself, who is a member of the Supreme Command. He is supposed to report if he has some questions for President Karadzic, not I as head of the RJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the MUP wasn't a junta that had some huge conflict with President Karadzic and wouldn't meet with him. I'll tell you and my friends won't contest it that it's in Mr. Karadzic's notebook that he met with Tomo Kovac on 13, 14, and 15 July. So what you know as a career military police officer in the MUP directly subordinated to Tomo Kovac, Tomo Kovac would have reported all the information he received to President Karadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: The minister's purview and actually the procedure is that the minister provides information collectively to the commander of the armed forces since there was a state of war that had been declared and also members of the government too. This is regular procedure according to the law, how information is supposed to be provided by the Ministry of the Interior to the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Could I have P04943, please. This is a 13 July document, the same day of the document we were talking about showing that prisoners were being taken by the MUP. This is to the police forces command staff Pale. It talks at the top about information on 10.000 able-bodied Muslims from the Srebrenica area gathered in Susnjari. And at the bottom of the page it talks about Zulfo Tursunovic and his movements and he's in the general sector of Snagovo, and it talks about Ibrahim Mandzic and where he's moving. So you at the police force's command staff in Pale would have gotten this information as well from this chief of administration, Todor Cikavic [phoen], correct, and try to keep your answer short, please, whether you got this or not.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: At the staff in Pale I don't remember this dispatch at all and I cannot confirm, really. On the one hand it was a long time ago and on the other hand I had my own duties in the staff that had to do with Sarajevo not in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: P05099, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And again, you said you barely ever got them. Think about that answer. This is another RDB report that goes up somewhere to where you were part of the staff. Take a look at this one carefully, please, 13 July 1995, very urgent. Bijeljina RJB at the top, that's you. It's type-signed by you. It say: "According to information available to the RDB, a Muslim group led by Zulfo Tursunovic ...," et cetera, and it says "is currently in the Snagovo sector." This document is being sent by you to the Zvornik CJB chief, Dragomir Vasic. So you're not just not -- you're not just getting information; you're acting on it and you're passing it on about Srebrenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I remember this dispatch because at that moment I appeared in that area because of negotiations. And when the column got out to exchange prisoner -- a policeman who had been taken prisoner and he was from the PJP Doboj. There was also the possibility that these forces would enter the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is the 13th of July, sir. You were in Zvornik on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. Mistake. I was in Zvornik on the 16th. Well, you know what? It's really been a long time, I really cannot link up all the dates, but this dispatch was sent to the chief, very urgent, because these are force that are coming and you can see that these are big forces coming in to big groups. And I wanted to say that when I arrived I saw them leaving, they were on the move and there was this possibility of them jeopardising the town of Zvornik. So that's why this very urgent dispatch was sent to the chief of the centre, so that he would be informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So you have available to you and you act on information about the movements of the Muslim column. That's important information. You also had information that the MUP was taking large numbers of prisoners. If you need me to go through all the evidence with you, I will. But there's evidence in this case that the MUP escorted thousands of prisoners and provided security to thousands of prisoners being transported from Bratunac to Zvornik on the 14th. So you knew about that as well, didn't you, the transport of prisoners to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No, no, absolutely not. I don't know when the MUP took prisoners and how. Again, I'm saying I'm not aware of these details that you are putting to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: P02987, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know Ljubisa Borovcanin personally I suppose in some capacity?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. This is his report from 13 July 1995, the same day as the other reports we've been looking at. This goes to the Pale police staff. It talks about the operation in Potocari which I won't go into. Page 2 of the English, please: "In the night between 12 and 13 July 1995, this armed Muslim group launched an attack in the direction of Konjevic Polje. In the combat that lasted several hours and which continued through today, the enemy had more than 200 dead, and we captured or had surrendered to us around 1500 Muslim soldiers. The number increases by the hour." This goes to the Pale police staff where we saw the other documents had gone to, some of which reached you. So you did know that on the 13th the MUP had taken 1500 prisoners approximately and was taking more; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That's not right. This is a special police brigade, that's what it says in the heading of the dispatch, and they are informing the police staff in Pale. You see that there, Vogosca, and special brigade Janja and Ljubisa Borovcanin, the deputy commander, is under the direct control, as far as combat activities are concerned, under the minister of the interior and he is not reporting to Milenko Karisik as head of the RJB. He is informing the staff headed by Tomo Kovac, who is deciding on behalf of the staff in Pale, that is to say that special brigade of the police is directly linked to the minister of the interior, not to the department, the RJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not talking about who he is linked to. I'm saying you got this information. We saw at the beginning you were number two of the persons listed on this staff.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but I do not read all dispatches. I'm out on the ground by Trnovo, the municipality of Sarajevo, and so on, so I did not see this dispatch. It was probably sent to the staff, as noted here, but I did not see this dispatch and in this chaos in relation to Sarajevo I didn't have time to react. This was the duty of the Chief of Staff, especially the special brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. You keep saying what your duty is not. I'm not asking you what your duty is. I'm asking you what you were informed of. And again, you're a top career professional law enforcement officer. The Srebrenica campaign is a hugely significant campaign, and your testimony is that you didn't read urgent dispatches to you and other dispatches to you during that operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, that is my testimony because at that time at that staff I was working on the Sarajevo front, not Srebrenica, and the staff was established for the Sarajevo front. As for decisions, to use the police forces, it is the minister who is supposed to decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, okay. So the special police commander knows they're taking thousands of prisoners. Dragomir Vasic knows that they're taking prisoners. Tomo Kovac knows that they're taking prisoners. People above you, below you know about these prisoners being taken. Dragan Kijac in state security at your level knows. So you're the only senior law enforcement officer in the MUP who doesn't know about prisoners being taken as far as you know; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That's right --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- that's right, because I had a specific task at the staff in Pale and the minister's powers came to the fore as regards decision-making about using the police in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me tell you -- let me see some other -- tell you about the Muslims going to Zvornik. Very briefly as you sit here today, before today did you know that Muslims were transported from Bratunac to Zvornik on 14 July? Or is that news to you today?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I did not deal with Srebrenica. Activities of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop, stop --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- ministry of the interior will --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. Answer my question. Listen carefully to the question. The question was: Before today, before you sat here today, did you know that Muslims were transported in large numbers from Bratunac to Zvornik on 14 July? The question is: Did you know it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember that. To this day I don't know what happened in Srebrenica, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I won't spend a lot of time on it, but witnesses in this trial, Milorad Brcakovic [phoen], who was Drago Nikolic's driver in Zvornik, met the convoy of buses on the 14th in Zvornik and he said there were policemen on the buses, civilian policemen, wearing blue uniforms. Another witness KDZ407 was present when prisoners were brought on the 14th to the Orahovac school in Zvornik. He guarded them there and he said - this is at P00379 at 6446 and onwards - that there were policemen wearing blue uniform and that they assisted in bringing the prisoners into the school. And he said that the policemen, the civilian policemen, who he recognised some of them from Zvornik, went back and forth with the buses. So these are civilian policemen, public security policemen, they're in your department. They are going with the prisoners from Bratunac to Zvornik to the detention sites. So you knew less than a uniformed policeman in Zvornik as head of the RJB; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That is quite natural because I was not there and I wasn't commanding that unit, that is to say these are questions for the head of the centre whose unit of the PJP was engaged there. As for details regarding that operation in Srebrenica, if it can be called that, I am hardly familiar with that because, I repeat once again, as head of the RJB I also dealt with this peace time work, if you will, within Republika Srpska and especially I was linked to the Sarajevo staff. So that part Mr. Kovac, I mean, and so on, they can explain that as witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Last question on this topic. Dragomir Vasic, the Zvornik centre chief, is in Bratunac on the 14th when the convoy leaves. Mane Djuric on the 14th is in Zvornik when the convoy arrives. So number 1 and number 2 of the Zvornik centre are at the beginning and the end of the convoy. None of that reaches you as head of the RJB from these public security subordinates of yours?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That's right --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- no. Report-wise, possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you're -- okay, well did you get reports? I thought you just said you didn't know until now that Muslims were brought from Bratunac to Zvornik on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No, I did not know that and I repeat once again that since I did not take part in that area in the capacity of chief of the RJB, I've already referred to the obligations that I had in that period of time as far as I can remember, and that was outside that area, except for when the column was leaving when I appeared in the area, because I was there for the exchange of the policemen and that is 100 kilometres away from there. As for the rest, the police, the reporting, and so on --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- the minister, the person who was minister then could say more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. On the 16th of July, what time did you set out to Zvornik on order of Mr. Kovac and your mission was to try to help, one, get -- get some MUP members who had been captured released? What time did you go to Zvornik on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I cannot remember the time because I could barely remember when it was mentioned that it was that date, the 16th. But I came, say, in the morning, it could have been the morning but I really cannot remember the time, and I stayed at the IKM for a long time --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- because the procedure of negotiating was long and unsuccessful, if I can put it that way --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. The question was when you went, okay, not how long you stayed or what you did. So you don't remember. Sometime in the morning, you think?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. Could you please repeat it for me --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- when I came or when I left?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When did you drive to Zvornik from Bijeljina on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I cannot remember the time exactly, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. When did you drive back?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I think it was in the afternoon, but I cannot remember the exact time either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And even though you've got nothing to do with Srebrenica, you're dealing with these humanitarian affairs in Sarajevo or something, Tomo Kovac gives you this one specific assignment, right, to go down there and try to get the MUP who've been captured by the Muslims released?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Just before --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, we have to 20 after, right, Your Honour? P04981, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is a document from the 15 July from RDB head Dragan Kijac. Oh, it's the day before you went down. I think my friends will stipulate it was the 16th that you were there. And on the top it talks how on the 14th of July the commander of the platoon from the Doboj SJB and another six members of the MUP and VRS were captured. So that's what this is about, right, trying to get those men released?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I was told that one policeman had been taken prisoner --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- a policeman from PJP Doboj and I went for him. I cannot remember any others now. I just remember this one policeman --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- that I waited for three or four hours, I think, but he did not get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. This is to you personally; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, I didn't even manage to read this, believe me --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: -- give me time to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Look at the top. RJB public security department head personally, that's you; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, that is I personally. That's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you can read it if you want. Let's scroll down to the bottom: "On the morning of 15th of July, a group of about a hundred captured Muslims from Srebrenica managed to escape from Gornja Pilica, Zvornik municipality." So you did receive information that there were prisoners in Zvornik, correct, the day before you went there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P04941, please, e-court page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be the last question for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, while it's coming up, you drove down there -- just to see the route you would take to the IKM. Bijeljina, it's above Pilica, so you would have come down through Pilica, through Rocevic, through Kozluk, to Karakaj, turned right, and then head towards the IKM; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Probably. To this day I wouldn't find my way on that road, I mean had somebody showed me the way to the IKM where Commander Pandurevic was. Even on the map I cannot show the exact route that I had taken, but I was in that area in some hills up there. I don't even know the exact location. I don't know what the name is. So after all this time I'm not sure which road it was, but I did arrive from Bijeljina. I think they told me -- actually, I even think there was somebody with me, I cannot remember, and showed me which way I was supposed to go to the IKM. Possibly it might have been Vasic, but I cannot remember exactly. But I was there at that time. I've remembered the date now as well, although it's been a very long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll get to that on Tuesday, because Vasic does confirm that he was with you. So we'll talk about that, but this route you took, you drove through Pilica where there were mass executions. You drove -- it's not right on the road, past Branjevo, you drove past Rocevic. You drove past Kozluk where there were mass executions on the 15th. You would have gone by Orahovac where there were mass executions on the 14th and you did it all again in reverse. So you basically went down this murder alley almost there and back on the 16th; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That is not correct. I don't know exactly where these places or execution sites were, and I did not see anyone there. I didn't see any corpses because I was in a vehicle. I didn't see any corpses. As far as I can remember today, I went along a clear road. I did not see anything on either side and I did not know of any of this that you are imputing to me right now, whatever you called it, murder alley. What you are saying to me now is not proper, that I went to all these execution sites and then went for the exchange? Absolutely not. I did not see any corpses along that road up to these hills, and you are referring to a route that I cannot confirm. To this day I would not be able to find my way if I didn't have a guide. Nobody took me to any execution sites. I went straight to the IKM of the Zvornik Brigade so that we could try to negotiate with the other side to get the imprisoned policemen from PJP Doboj released. That's the only thing I can say and I do not accept as a fact any of the rest. I do not accept it as the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll adjourn for today and continue Tuesday, next week, at 9.00. Mr. Karisik, I'd like to advise you not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony while you are giving evidence. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
